Teamcenter\-X Procedures

# <a id="_Toc139976035"></a>Access Control

The document is a formal procedure to outline working agreement for managing and auditing the Access to GITLab, AWS Secrets Vault and Splunk accounts based on job role and Least Privilege\.

##### Policy Tag

[Siemens Industry Software \(SISW\) SaaS Access Control Policy\.pdf](#_References)

##### Scope

This document defines the procedure for teams to access and grant permissions to system resources used for Teamcenter\-X Development\. Individual teams may follow specialized procedures that implement these in more detail or in an automated matter\. These procedures are the responsibility of the individual teams\.

This document includes the procedure to grant and revoke access to the following resources:

- GitLab
- AWS Deployment Accounts
- AWS Federated Production Accounts
- Splunk Dashboard
- Secrets Vault

## <a id="_Toc139976036"></a>Principles of access control in Teamcenter X

1. Access to information and information processing facilities shall be controlled based on the following:

- Business requirements
- Security requirements
- Asset management policy
- Need\-to\-know basis
- Descriptions of user access levels and roles
- Deprovisioning processes

1. Granting access to assets controlled by Teamcenter X the responsibility of the development managers\.
2. Through an onboarding process, members joining the Teamcenter X team will be granted access to assets based on need\-to\-know basis and level of access needed\. Request to grant access is managed by the Team leaders and Scrum masters according the procedure in the following sections, for AWS accounts and using Service Now for Git Repo Account\.
3. Members from the following organizations will be granted access:

- TCX \- CloudART members: developers, architects, managers
- non\-TCX, LCS members from development teams that contribute to TCX Solutions, integrations and Add\-ons
- TCX, CApS/GDN members from the external to LCS development teams that contribute to TCX or required to consume code from TCX\.

1. An offboarding process revokes all the privileges and accounts provided to the user when the user exits the Teamcenter X team\.
2. Automated processes will be enabled wherever possible to force users to regenerate access keys and passwords\.
3. The systems themselves serve as system\-of\-record with the addition of email approval from management\.

### Development Authorization Principles

1. Only users having GitLab Maintainer role are permitted to generate release artifacts for consumption of CApS team\.
2. Development managers control assignment of federated user roles to members in Teamcenter X\. Federated users are not AWS account users, they are Siemens Users connected to the AWS account through AWS SSO\.

*Note: Definition of Federated Users in AWS: Federated users \(external identities\) are users you manage outside of AWS in your corporate directory, but to whom you grant access to your AWS account using temporary security credentials\. They differ from IAM users, which are created and maintained in your AWS account\.*

1. Only federated users are allowed to share Teamcenter release artifacts through controlled AWS S3 buckets with CApS team\.
2. Federated users are responsible to control and manage, Audit logging, encryption at rest and versioning on Amazon S3 buckets shared with CApS team\.

### Access review cadence

1. A periodic review of not later than 3 months will be conducted to audit user access to controlled assets\.
2. Responsible parties will review an Access Control Register that consolidates current records from AWS and GitLab\. Additionally the responsible parties will review records from Ansible and Vault\.

## Procedure to Grant or Revoke access to GitLab

### Procedure to request GitLab license \(and thereby gain overall access\)

1. The employee or delegate raises a Gitlab License Request using the service\-now portal: [DISW: GitLab License Request Form](https://diswsiemens.service-now.com/sp?id=sc_cat_item&sys_id=b9e8ac1397b91550d17af580f053afe3&sysparm_category=f28707be1b954cd02bc0dac7bd4bcbd6) 

![](data:image/png;base64,)

1. For Teamcenter X the applicable instance of GitLab is “https://gitlab\.industrysoftware\.automation\.siemens\.com\(Milford\)”
2. With the request one mail will be sent to Manager for the approval\.
3. Manager will approve the request and access will be granted\. Team member will get a mail for the access\.

*![Warning with solid fill](data:image/png;base64,)*

__Note__

*This procedure is applicable to the enterprise version of Git which is being used by DI SW\. The other Gitlab is also used as Siemens internal repo of projects at “code\.siemens\.com”\. The access to “code\.siemens\.com” is available to all the Siemens Employees\. The Repo specific access procedure to both Enterprise Gitlab and “code\.siemens\.com” is similar as explained in sections below\.*

### <a id="_Toc136594030"></a>Procedure to provide access to TcX GitLab project repository

1. Team members can be added to the entire TcX Gitlab Group, or can be added to specific repositories\. In either case the requester sends an email to the manager requesting access; if approved the manager forwards the request to the repository or group administrator\. 

__Email Format:__

To

<Employee Manager>

Mail Subject

TCX: Request access to GitLab Project\(s\)

Mail Body

Please grant me access to the GitLab project\(s\) for *<Development/View\-only>* purpose\.

*Note: <Reason>: can be development or view\-only\.*

*<Manager’s Email>: Will be your current manager’s siemens email address\. For example, deepesh\.jain@siemens\.com for RapidStart team\.*

1. Manager will approve and forward it to GitLab Admin team member\(s\) to provide access\.

*![Warning with solid fill](data:image/png;base64,)*

__Note__

*GitLab Admins are the team members who have GitLab Access as “Owner” of the repo\. Each of the Scrum have few team members as “Owner”\. The other available roles are Guest, Reporter, Developer, and Maintainer\. Refer ”[https://docs\.gitlab\.com/ee/user/permissions\.html](https://docs.gitlab.com/ee/user/permissions.html)” for more details on permissions of these roles\.*

1. The GitLab Admin team member will grant access to the appropriate team member with the required role and mail the same\.
2. Team member will get email notification once the access is provided\.

### Procedure to revoke access to specific repository

Removing a team member from a group or repository is a matter of emailing the administrator

### Procedure to revoke access to Gitlab

When an employee leaves the company, the manager must raise a ticket in SNOW\. The ticket type is “incident”:

### Procedure to request access to Security and Access Management \(SAM\) accounts

1. Security and Access Management \(SAM\) account is used for volume storage and SSO logins for Teamcenter X users\. It provides the webkey authentications\.
2. To request access to SAM account Team member will send an email to manager for getting the access\.

To

<Employee’s Manager’s email>

Mail Subject

TCX: Request access to SAM account\(s\)

Mail Body

Please grant me access to the SAM accounts for doing development/testing activities\.

  


1. After receiving the email the Manager or the Admin in the team grant access to SAM account to the user\.

## <a id="_Toc139976041"></a>Procedure to provide access to Secrets Vault

TcX leverages secrets vault for housing confidential credentials, etc, that are used by TcX automation scripts\. Using the secrets vault is largely token\-based\. Tokens are expired and regenerated on a monthly basis and shared with Scrum Masters, who are responsible to distribute the token to their team on an as\-needed bases\.

A limited number of employees have username/password\-based access to the top\-level vault namespace and have admin permissions\. To grant or revoke access the following procedures are required\.

To

<Employee’s Manager’s email>

Mail Subject

TCX: Request admin access to Secrets Vault

Mail Body

Please grant me administrative access to the overall Secrets Vault\. I need this because <reason>\.

*![Warning with solid fill](data:image/png;base64,)*

__Note__

*Here, <Manager’s Email>: Will be your current manager’s siemens email address\. \(Team Manager here are the manager and the Scrum Masters of TcX Projects\.\)*

If approved, the manager shall send an approval email to the Vault Administrators with the following information:

- Requester’s vault username
- Requester’s email address
- Justification

*The current procedure for Vault Administration is in flux as the development integrating Vault has recently begun*

## <a id="_Toc139976043"></a>Procedure to review of access rights

All the stakeholders responsible for granting and revoking access shall attend the Quarterly Access Review to ensure that the appropriate action is taken to remove unnecessary access and there is no privilege creep\. A quarterly call shall be organized to achieve this\. The following shall be in the agenda of the call

1. List of employees who have resigned from the team\.
2. List of employees with changed privileges\.
3. List of employees who have moved to another department\.
4. Any new access requirements granted during the quarter including temporary accounts, audit accounts etc\.

The Team shall review the access rights of all employees and ensure that no privilege access is left unmonitored\. The team may leverage different data sources and will document their findings, including the option to create MyPolarion tasks\.
